articles.headline: Wall Street ends higher as Amazon soothes AI jitters
articles.summary: STORY: Wall Street ended higher on Friday, with the Dow adding more than half a percent, the S&P 500 gaining seven-tenths of a percent and the Nasdaq climbing one percent.:: AmazonAmazon surged more than 15% after the tech giant posted its biggest quarterly revenue growth in over four years. Its results, along with a similar report from Microsoft this week, alleviated investor concerns about potential overspending on AI data centers.Meanwhile, shares of Apple tumbled more than 7% after a disappointing forecast showed that the iPhone maker was struggling to secure enough components, as the AI-driven data center boom strains global supply chains.Friday marked the end of a bumpy week for stocks that included a Fed policy meeting in which the central bank left rates unchanged - but with three dissenters pushing for a 25 basis point hike.Dean Smith is chief strategist & portfolio manager at FolioBeyond."I think there was a decent case to be made that a hike is in order. Inflation, we had a slightly softer print on the most recent one, but inflation is now running well above Fed's 2% stated target. It's higher now than it was a year ago and it seems to be reaccelerating. [FLASH] So it was a close call probably, but I think, you know, if I had been on that voting committee, I would have voted for a rate hike as well.":: ArchiveOther stocks on the move Friday included Monolithic Power Systems, which rose more than 8% after forecasting third-quarter revenue above estimates.But shares of GoDaddy slid nearly 17% after the domain registrar narrowed its annual revenue forecast.

articles.headline: Market Talk: Apple sinks, Amazon soars in split verdict on AI winners
articles.summary: STORY: :: Recorded on July 31:: Lisa Bernhard, Reuters:: Dean Smith, Portfolio Manager, FolioBeyondShares of Apple tumbled as much as 10% on Friday after a disappointing forecast showed that the iPhone maker was struggling to secure enough components as the AI-driven data center boom strains global supply chains.The drop, if sustained, would erase nearly $500 billion from Apple's market capitalization and return the crown of the world's most valuable company to AI chip giant Nvidia, days after reclaiming it.Meanwhile, shares of Amazon soared as much as 15% after the tech giant's solid cloud sales growth reinforced investor confidence in its massive AI bets."There's two really different trends going on," said Smith. "One is the hardware constraint, the [other is] cloud compute capacity, and those are going to continue to drive what we see in the AI investment thesis."Next week, the focus will remain on AI when SpaceX delivers its first quarterly earnings results since going public."There's no mystery about how many rockets they're firing off, we can see them," said Dean with a laugh. "So what I'm looking for in SpaceX is to see what is their plan for the AI side of the business."

articles.headline: Amazon's Zoox wins first US approval for driverless robotaxis
articles.summary: STORY: :: ArchiveWhat if your next driverless taxi had no steering wheel? That may soon become a reality.Amazon-owned Zoox has won the first U.S. approval for commercial deployment of a robotaxi built without traditional human controls.The approval came from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, or NHTSA...allowing the company to begin charging for rides in Las Vegas once it completes state requirements.Here's NHTSA administrator Jonathan Morrison."Since our standards get into performance requirements for specific aspects such as braking performance, they provided information and we received public comment, and we made that determination that their vehicle as equipped, can meet all of those requirements and in fact, exceed those."The vehicle looks very different from a conventional car.It's an electric, carriage-style robotaxi with two rows of inward-facing seats and a top speed of 75 miles per hour.Federal officials say Zoox can deploy up to 2,500 vehicles in each of the next two years.The move comes as companies including Alphabet's Waymo and Elon Musk's Tesla race to expand driverless ride-hailing services across the U.S.The green light comes with added oversight.U.S. regulators say the firm must report issues including crashes and inappropriate stops.Authorities also retain the power to revoke the exemption if major safety concerns emerge.

articles.headline: Amazon reports strong profits and net sales for Q2, fueled by robust growth in cloud computing unit
articles.summary: Amazon delivered strong profits and net sales during its fiscal second quarter, helped by surging growth in its prominent cloud computing unit.  The e-commerce and technology company said Thursday that sales in its cloud computing unit called AWS rose 37% during the April-June period, faster than the 28% clip in the previous quarter and marking the fastest rate of growth in 18 quarters.  In a statement released Thursday, Amazon's CEO and president Andy Jassy said AWS is “booming” and noted that its AI and chips businesses each eclipsed run rates of more than $25 billion.
